name: Daisy Defect Does Not Exponentially Control Yang Depth
statement: There is no universal exponential lower bound on daisy completion defect in terms of Yang depth: the classes $E_k$ satisfy $\sigma(E_k)=3$, $\delta_{\mathrm{CM},K}(E_k)=k+1$, and $\delta_D(E_k)\leq2k+1$.
proof: The concepts have disjoint two-element supports, so pairwise disagreements have size four. Their downward completion adds the empty support and all singletons. The higher-agreement complexes are simplex skeleta, with the boundary at the terminal rank giving depth defect $k+1$.
comments: These witnesses are disconnected and are not partial cubes for $k>1$.
